title: Promatch: Extending the Reach of Real-Time Quantum Error Correction with Adaptive Predecoding
problem: Real-time MWPM decoders for quantum error correction are limited to distance d=9 because the Hamming weight of syndromes exceeds their decoding capacity. Extending to larger distances requires handling higher-weight syndromes while maintaining sub-microsecond latency on superconducting quantum processors.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires real-time quantum error correction to prevent error backlogs, but current decoders are limited in the logical qubit distances they can support.
method: Promatch adds a preprocessing step called adaptive predecoding that takes error patterns (called syndromes, which is the fingerprint of where errors occurred in the quantum system) and simplifies them by reducing the number of individual errors in each pattern. Once simplified, these patterns can be handled by existing fast decoders called real-time MWPM decoders (which find the most likely way to correct errors), which normally fail when patterns have too many errors. This lets quantum error correction work on larger systems while keeping everything fast—decision time stays under a microsecond.
key_novelty: Using adaptive predecoding (a preprocessing step that reduces the number of errors in error patterns) as a first step allows existing real-time quantum error decoders to handle larger systems, extending beyond distance 9.
contributions: Adaptive predecoding algorithm for reducing syndrome Hamming weight
Extension of real-time MWPM decoders to support larger quantum error correction distances
Demonstration that predecoding maintains sub-microsecond latency for higher-distance codes
